message_1_subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive eval & cost/TCO - next steps
message_1_body:
Hi Julia --

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the competitive / cost notes we promised on the call: see bullets and the ask at the end.

Call takeaways:
- Primary use-case: low-latency question-answering for product docs (avg prompt ~450 tokens, responses ~350 tokens), ~200k monthly active users, expected 2-3 requests/user/day variable.
- Key constraints: 200ms median latency target for interactive flows; strong need for data residency in US; procurement will want TCO and a short PoC.

High-level unit economics (rough estimates to inform PoC scope):
- Redwood Hosted (shared, optimized open models + caching): ~$18 per 1M tokens list pricing. With expected prefix/KV cache hit ~40% (doc-heavy QA), effective cost ~= $11/1M tokens.
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity w/ tuned batching & quantization): ~$12 per 1M tokens at our projected utilization for CloudServe workload; with caching could go down to ~$7-8/1M.
- AWS / Hyperscaler endpoints (reference pricing for comparable generation): AWS Bedrock / SageMaker endpoints: ~$38-45 per 1M tokens (varies by model and gen path).
- Google Vertex AI: ~$35-40 per 1M tokens (proprietary models).

Why these numbers matter: caching (prefix/KV) and batching are the biggest levers for lowering unit cost on doc QA workloads. Example: if you hit 40% prefix cache, you avoid repeated encoder + partial decode costs on common query prefixes; batching helps amortize per-request overhead but increases tail latency if not controlled.

Recommended next tests for a focused PoC (proposed):
1) Cold vs warm cache run: 100k generated tokens worth of representative queries to measure cache hit delta and effective cost.
2) Batch sizing sensitivity: run with batch sizes 1, 4, 8 to capture throughput vs p95 latency tradeoffs.
3) Quantization/profile check on Dedicated: run same workload on our int8 quantized profile to capture CPU/GPU utilization and delta in tokens/sec.

Acceptance criteria for PoC:
- Median latency < 250ms for interactive path at target concurrency (we can align on concurrency numbers),
- Effective cost < $15 per 1M tokens (hosted) or < $10 per 1M tokens (dedicated) after accounting for measured cache hits,
- Data residency & audit logs validated for US region.

Next steps / asks:
- If you can share a ~1k-sample of typical prompts + expected response lengths (or let us replay a sanitized subset), we can run the cold/warm cache tests on Redwood and share the TCO spreadsheet.
- Are procurement and security the right folks to loop in? I copied Aditya to help with pricing/contract questions.

I attached a short one-pager and will upload a detailed TCO workbook after we align on sample access. Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up this week to confirm PoC scope.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin

message_2_subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive eval & cost/TCO - next steps
message_2_body:
Thanks Marcus -- this is helpful and in the right ballpark. A few clarifying Qs before we hand this to procurement: 

1) How sensitive are those effective cost numbers to cache hit rate? If our real-world cache is 25% vs your 40%, what does that look like?
2) For the Dedicated $12/1M estimate, what commitment level is assumed (hours/throughput)?
3) We need to confirm US data residency and SOC 2 scope before legal will sign off. Can you share your SOC 2 + data retention docs?

Procurement (cc'd) -- we may want Redwood to provide the PoC under a short MSA or an NDA-first scoped SOW.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow morning if that helps.

Best,
Julia Park
Head of Product Integrations | CloudServe Inc
julia@cloudserve.com
message_3_subject: Re: Follow-up: Competitive eval & cost/TCO - next steps
message_3_body:
Julia -- quick answers and next steps (see attached TCO workbook draft):

1) Cache sensitivity: we modeled three scenarios in the attached workbook: 20%, 40%, 60% prefix/KV hit rates. At 20% your effective hosted cost moves from ~$11/1M (40% case) to ~$14.5/1M; at 60% it drops to ~$8/1M. The workbook includes token-level line items so you can plug in your observed hit rates.

2) Dedicated assumptions: $12/1M assumes a 6-month reserved slot at 70% average utilization for the target model (4x A10-style instances equivalent in our config). We can provide a lower committed rate for 12- or 24-month terms; Aditya (cc) can share commitment tiers and committed throughput numbers.

3) Compliance docs: attaching SOC 2 summary & we will share the full report under NDA. Data residency: we support US-only private deployments (VPC) for production; hosted options can be restricted to US regions and we emit audit logs and retention controls.

Proposed PoC plan (timeline):
- Day 0: sign mutual NDA / short SOW (we can use our standard PoC SOW).
- Day 1-3: you share 1k-sample prompts or we provide a sanitizer + loader.
- Day 4-6: Redwood runs cold vs warm cache tests and batch sensitivity runs; we produce a measurement pack (latency, throughput, GPU utilization, cache hit curves) and fill the TCO workbook.
- Day 7: 30-min review with CloudServe and procurement to go over results and next commercial recommendation.

Acceptance criteria and go/no-go gates are in the workbook. If that sounds good I can have the NDA + PoC SOW over to procurement by EOD.

Thanks -- looping Aditya for contractual and pricing details.

--Marcus
